The finite nodes yield a Vandermonde matrix, with local sharpness on the fixed-product distinct-root manifold by the inverse/implicit function theorems. Just above the first threshold r=a+epsilon<sqrt(2)a, exactly 2m disjoint coordinate caps contribute; beta integral integral_0^1 v(1-v)^((d-1)/2)dv=4/((d+1)(d+3)) gives exponent and coefficient, including m/2 in d=3. Independent 2D direct polar integration reproduced pi*r^2/(ab)-4*r^3(a+b)/(3a^2b^2)+r^4/(2a^2b^2). This does not assert large-radius finite-sample uniqueness or reconstruct general convex bodies.
